problem: Let ${v}_{1}=[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ and ${v}_{2}=[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]$ be eigenvectors of a matrix $A$ that correspond to eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1}=1$ and ${\lambda }_{2}=-1,$ respectively. What is the general solution of the matrix differential equation ${x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t)?$
worked_solution:
Given a system of first-order linear ODEs in the form

$$
{x}^{′}(t)=Ax(t),
$$

where $A$ has two distinct eigenvalues ${\lambda }_{1},{\lambda }_{2}$ with corresponding eigenvectors ${v}_{1}$ and ${v}_{2},$ the formula for the general solution is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}{v}_{1}{e}^{{\lambda }_{1}t}+{c}_{2}{v}_{2}{e}^{{\lambda }_{2}t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$

Therefore, the general solution of our matrix differential equation is

$$
x(t)={c}_{1}[\begin{aligned}-2 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{t}+{c}_{2}[\begin{aligned}0 \\ 1\end{aligned}]{e}^{-t},\,{c}_{1},{c}_{2}\in R.
$$
